title: Smooth rational-point orbits over arbitrary fields
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] with an action $a:G\times_k X\to X$, meaning a morphism satisfying the unit and multiplication identities; products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $x\in X(k)$ write $b_x:G\to X$ for $g\mapsto a(g,x)$. The image $b_x(|G|)$ is locally closed in $|X|$; thus $U=X\setminus(\overline{b_x(|G|)}\setminus b_x(|G|))$ is an open subscheme of $X$ in which $b_x(|G|)$ is closed. Let $O_x$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme of $U$ on $b_x(|G|)$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme], and $i:O_x\to X$ its inclusion, an immersion (a closed immersion into an open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]). There is a factorization $b_x=i\circ\beta$ with $\beta:G\to O_x$ flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The scheme $O_x$ is smooth over $k$. Neither connectedness of $G$, perfection of $k$, nor reducedness of $X$ is required; the orbit morphism $\beta$ need not be smooth.

source.place: Section 7.c, locally closed orbit paragraph and Proposition 7.4(b), printed pp.139--140, using Proposition 1.65(c); Proposition 7.17, printed p.143. Local finite presentation follows from finite type over the locally Noetherian orbit; it does not assert smoothness of the orbit morphism.

proof.text: Put $b=b_x$ and $S=b(|G|)$; the identity of $G$ shows $S\ne\varnothing$. Finite-type schemes over a field are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The map $b$ is finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], since $G$ is finite type over $k$ and $X$ is separated. We will also use this for the factor maps to separated locally closed subschemes of $X$. Closed subschemes are finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c); opens of Noetherian schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], hence their inclusions are quasi-compact and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Composition and base change preserve finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Thus all these schemes and their scalar extensions are Noetherian and finite type over the relevant field. Every finite-type map between them is locally finitely presented: on affine charts its target ring is Noetherian and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] applies. All such maps are quasi-separated: their diagonals have Noetherian source, so the inverse image of an affine open is quasi-compact.

The smooth $G$ is geometrically reduced, hence reduced, by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $b$. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], it is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline S$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], the factor map $h:G\to Z$ is scheme-theoretically dominant, with injective structure-sheaf map. It is quasi-compact by step 1, since $Z$ is separated (its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X$). Apply [lem-sbc-geometrically-reduced-dominant-descent] to $h$ and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its source is geometrically reduced, so $Z$ is geometrically reduced. This is the geometric reducedness needed below; reducedness over an imperfect field alone would not suffice.

source.place: Proposition 7.4(b), pp.139--140, injective structure-sheaf argument; Stacks 056T, 056B and 081I.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $K/k$, and use a subscript $K$ for scalar extension [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-base-change]. On affine charts, the projection from scalar extension is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Hence [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback], applied to $h:G\to Z$, says that $h_K:G_K\to Z_K$ is scheme-theoretically dominant. All quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses were checked in step 1. Therefore [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] identifies $|Z_K|$ with the closure of $S_K:=b_K(|G_K|)$ in $|X_K|$. Moreover $Z_K$ and $G_K$ are reduced by step 2. Set-theoretically $S_K=p^{-1}(S)$ for $p:X_K\to X$: for each $y\in X_K$ above $z\in S$, the nonempty fibre $b^{-1}(z)$ stays nonempty after the field extension $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(y)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applied to its map onto $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$; the converse follows by composition.

Over $K$, Chevalley [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] makes $S_K$ constructible. The target is qcqs and $b_K$ is quasi-compact and locally finitely presented by step 1. Choose an affine open $A\subset X_K$ meeting $Z_K$. The nonempty constructible subset $S_K\cap A$ is dense in $Z_K\cap A$, so [lem-wf-affine-constructible-open](2) gives a nonempty open $W\subset Z_K$ contained in $S_K$. For $g\in G(K)$, translation $t_g$ on $X_K$ has inverse $t_{g^{-1}}$, and $t_gb_K=b_KL_g$ by the action identities [def-sc-group-scheme]. Thus $t_g$ preserves $S_K$ and its closure. The union $V=\bigcup_{g\in G(K)}t_gW$ is open in $Z_K$ and contained in $S_K$. Choose $w\in W(K)$ and a lift $u\in G(K)$ of $w$. Such points exist: nonempty finite-type schemes over $K$ have closed points by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and their residue fields are $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]; this applies also to the fibre over $w$. For every closed $v\in G_K$, $b_K(v)=t_{vu^{-1}}w\in V$. Consequently the open $b_K^{-1}V$ contains every closed point of $G_K$, and the same Jacobson assertion gives $b_K^{-1}V=G_K$. Thus $S_K=V$ is open in $Z_K$.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(b), p.27, translates of a constructible interior; Stacks 054J and 0478.

proof.text: The one-point map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective and integral: every element of $K$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $k$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. It is universally closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. Its base change $p_Z:Z_K\to Z$ is closed and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Step 3 gives $p_Z^{-1}S=S_K$. Therefore $Z\setminus S=p_Z(Z_K\setminus S_K)$ is closed, since step 4 made $S_K$ open. This proves $S$ open in $\overline S$, hence locally closed in $X$. Its boundary $\overline S\setminus S$ is closed in $X$, so the stated $U=X\setminus(\overline S\setminus S)$ is open and $S$ is closed in $U$.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(b), p.27, quotient-map descent made explicit; Stacks 01WM, 01W4 and 01S1.

proof.text: Let $O$ be the open subscheme $S\subset Z$. In $U$, its inclusion is the restriction of the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$, so it is closed with image $S$ and is reduced. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) identifies it with the specified $O_x$. The factor map $h:G\to Z$ has image in this open, so restricts uniquely to $\beta:G\to O$, with $b=i\beta$ and $\beta$ surjective by the definition of $S$. It is finite type and locally finitely presented by step 1, since $O$ is separated over $k$. As an open subscheme of the geometrically reduced $Z$, $O$ is geometrically reduced (each scalar extension is an open of the reduced $Z_L$). In particular $O_K$ is the reduced induced locally closed subscheme on $S_K$. For $g\in G(K)$, the automorphism $t_g$ of $X_K$ preserves $S_K$ and $Z_K$; the same uniqueness of reduced closed structures, followed by open restriction, gives an automorphism of $O_K$. It satisfies $t_g\beta_K=\beta_KL_g$ by composing with the immersion into $X_K$, a monomorphism: open inclusions are monomorphisms and closed inclusions are so since locally their ring maps are surjective.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(c), p.27, reduced-image factorization; Stacks 01J3 and 01J4.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $B\subset O_K$. Its inverse image under the finite-type $\beta_K$ is quasi-compact, so it has a finite affine open cover $T_1,\ldots,T_r$. For each affine map $T_j\to B$, apply [lem-sfb-reduced-affine-generic-flat-finite-presentation]: the target $B$ is reduced, and the map is locally finite type by step 1. It supplies a dense open $D_j\subset B$ over which this map is flat. Their finite intersection $D$ is dense and nonempty in the nonempty $B$. Over $D$ every source point lies in some $T_j$, so all stalk maps for $\beta_K$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus $\beta_K$ is flat over the nonempty open $D\subset O_K$. No irreducibility or connectedness of $G_K$ or $O_K$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(a), p.27, generic flatness; Stacks 052B (proposition-generic-flatness-reduced), finite-affine-cover argument.

proof.text: Every closed point $y\in O_K$ is $K$-rational and has a lift $v\in G(K)$ under the surjective $\beta_K$, by the closed-point and fibre argument of step 4. Choose $d\in D(K)$ and $u\in G(K)$ with $\beta_K(u)=d$. Then $y=t_{vu^{-1}}d$. Hence the union of the open translates $t_gD$ contains every closed point of $O_K$ and equals $O_K$ by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. In the square $t_g\beta_K=\beta_KL_g$ both horizontal maps are isomorphisms by step 6, so their stalk-ring isomorphisms identify the stalk maps over $t_gD$ with those over $D$. Flatness is invariant under ring isomorphisms (the tensor functors are identified). Step 7 and [def-weil-flat-morphism] therefore show that $\beta_K$ is flat everywhere.

source.place: Proposition 1.65(a), p.27, translation of the flat open.

proof.text: To descend flatness, take affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset O$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset\beta^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. Step 8 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] say $A_K\to B_K$ is flat, where $A_K=A\otimes_kK$ and $B_K=B\otimes_kK$. Both $A\to A_K$ and $B\to B_K$ are faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp], $A\to B_K$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-algebra-faithfully-flat-descent] to $A\to B\to B_K$ to conclude $A\to B$ is flat. The affine criterion again gives flatness of $\beta$. Its surjectivity and local finite presentation were proved in step 6. Finally apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $G\xrightarrow\beta O\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: its composite is smooth by hypothesis, and $\beta$ is flat, surjective and locally finitely presented. Thus $O=O_x$ is smooth over $k$. This argument never asserts that $\beta$ itself is smooth.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 1.65(a)--(c), pp.26--27, and Proposition 7.4(b), pp.139--140; geometric-reducedness argument expanded using Stacks 081I and 056B; smoothness concluded by source descent 05B5.

Step 2: Z is geometrically reduced via scheme-image-ideal injectivity and dominant-descent. Step 3: dense-flat-pullback with h qcqs, and the fibre computation S_K = p^{-1}S via 01S1.
